name: Teraco DB1 (Riverhorse Valley, Durban)
notes: Teraco's Durban facility DB1 at Riverhorse Close, Riverhorse Valley, north Durban - largest data centre in KwaZulu-Natal; expansion (completed 2023) doubled capacity to 2.2MW critical power load, 5,800 sq m building, 700+ racks, 4MVA utility supply (per TechCentral/operator). Teraco official Durban page confirms vendor-neutral colocation; TelCables SA established a PoP at Teraco Riverhorse DB1 (2025-06-26, IOL) reinforcing hub status. name: OADC Durban (DUR1, Amanzimtoti)
developer: Open Access Data Centres (OADC) / WIOCC Group
notes: OADC Durban DUR1 at Arbour Junction 2, Arbour Road, Amanzimtoti (20km south of Durban CBD, eThekwini) - carrier-neutral Tier III-designed facility, 4,200 sq m with ~2,000 sq m IT white space; went live April 2022 with 4MW power capacity; serves as the Durban landing station for the 2Africa subsea cable (landed by WIOCC, one of 2Africa's four SA landings: Yzerfontein, Duynefontein, Gqeberha, Amanzimtoti). OADC hyperscale page confirms landing-station DC role.

name: OADC Umhlanga (former NTT Data SA / Internet Solutions facility)
developer: Open Access Data Centres (OADC) / WIOCC Group (formerly NTT Data SA / Internet Solutions)
notes: Legacy Internet Solutions/NTT Data SA facility at 3 Sugar Close, Umhlanga (eThekwini) - listed on DataCenterMap and PeeringDB as NTT DATA Umhlanga/Durban; OADC's acquisition of seven NTT Data SA centres (Bloemfontein, Cape Town, East London, Gqeberha, Umhlanga, Bryanston, Parklands) concluded 31 Dec 2025, so current owner is OADC. Directory-grade evidence only; no public MW capacity; small regional colocation/edge facility.

name: Dube TradePort data centre (La Mercy)
notes: Dube TradePort Corporation operates a data centre in its SEZ precinct at La Mercy, near King Shaka International Airport (eThekwini); a SABEN (SA NREN) RFQ sought a dark-fibre link between Teraco Durban DB1 and the Dube TradePort datacentre, confirming existence. No public MW capacity; likely modest government/SEZ facility supporting the aerotropolis.

name: eThekwini Korean AI Data Centre proposal (Amanzimtoti / Lovu River)
developer: eThekwini Municipality + Korea South Power Consortium (KOSPO-led)
notes: In early 2026 the Korea South Power Consortium approached eThekwini to build a multi-billion-rand AI data centre in Amanzimtoti (site at mouth of Lovu River near the Amanzimtoti cable landing station). eThekwini issued official 'Clarity' media statements addressing concerns; council approved an exploratory MOA - briefing documents referenced ~400MW (would be ~25% of Durban's electricity, US$3-10bn), but the municipality says MW figures are unconfirmed and the MOA is exploratory. Status per methodology: MOA/announced = lead, not yet land-use/EA/building-plan approved. Capacity 400MW as reported, unconfirmed.
